text:
Incident Bot: PAGER -> paging on-call: high request spike causing cascading fallbacks in smart-routing. initial detection 2815001228.

Maya: paging — seeing a huge increase in fallback-to-variant traffic, qps doubled in us-west-2. latency up and 503s starting to pile. dashboard: https://console.redwood/api/ops/alerts/2815

Leo: I'm on it, grabbing logs. initial hypothesis: client retries + failover to fallback variant creating a thundering herd.

Sam: confirm, traces show many clients got 503, immediate retry (no jitter), routed to fallback variant in region, which then started rejecting -> more retries.

Maya: impact: some customers report degraded responses; estimate ~8% of requests seeing >2x latency, 1.9% 5xx. customer-facing SLOs approaching threshold.

Ellen: which routing policy triggered? did we roll anything?

Leo: checking rollout history... 2814999000: routing policy change pushed to smart-routing v2: fallbackVariants weight set to 0.7 for us-west pref fallback. I see a bug: variant name mismatch in the policy (typo) so it fell back to the global fallback rule which triggers region hop.

Priya: so misnamed variant -> global fallback -> region fallback loop? explain the loop.

Sam: sequence: primary -> fail (503) -> client retries immediately -> smart-routing sees overload and tries region fallback -> fallback variant in other region overloaded -> fail -> clients retry again -> requests multiply. Also our 'circuit-breaker' threshold was too high for this pattern.

Maya: posting key logs:```
[2815001234] svc:router error: variant_not_found: v2-eng-quantized
[2815001234] fallback: routing to global-fallback:us-west-2
[2815001235] proxy: upstream 503 for model-serving-az1
[2815001236] client: immediate-retry detected for session=abc123 count=3
```

Incident Bot: action suggested by runbooks: (1) disable cross-region fallback, (2) apply edge rate-limit on retries, (3) remove/rollback erroneous routing policy.

Leo: I'm going to disable cross-region fallback policy now. will run:```bash
# disable global fallback routing
redwoodctl routing update --name smart-routing-v2 --set cross_region_fallback=false
```

Sam: I'll put a temporary 5rps per-ip retry throttle at the edge and enable exponential backoff enforcement.

Priya: Also push a canary to reduce fallback weight:```json
{"fallbackVariants": {"global-fallback": 0.1}}
```

Maya: executing rollback of the misconfigured policy (revert to 2814998000 state). patch now.

Ellen: I'm taking the pager at 2815001350, stand by. Maya please post confirmation once policy is reverted.

Maya: policy revert complete. routing diff: removed typo, fallback map restored. verified primary variants now get traffic.

Sam: edge rate-limit applied. logs show immediate drop in retry bursts. new incoming qps stabilized to expected baseline.

Leo: monitoring: 10m window after mitigations — error rate down from 1.9% to 0.3%, p99 latency back to normal range. traces show retries decreased by ~75%.

Priya: note for postmortem: root cause is twofold: (1) routing policy typo that routed to global fallback path, (2) clients using aggressive immediate retries (no jitter/exponential backoff). amplification happened because server failover increased surface area for retries.

Maya: mitigation summary posted to status page draft: "Deployed rollback of smart-routing policy and temporary edge retry throttles. Customers may have seen transient 503s while we mitigated. No data loss." Please review.

Ellen: taking over incident ops. next steps: run full traffic replay against staging to validate fallback behavior, add unit test to ensure variant name validation in routing policies, and set automatic rollback on variant-not-found errors.

Sam: action items assigned: Sam -> permanent retry-throttling and jitter enforcement at edge. Leo -> validation + CI gate for routing policy names. Maya -> postmortem writeup and customer comms. Priya -> add telemetry to detect retry amplification patterns and auto-toggle cross-region fallback.

Maya: add note: customer A reported a 30s window of degraded responses; ops team offered targeted support.

PagerDuty: Pager acknowledged by Ellen at 2815001350.

Incident Bot: incident escalated to SEV-2. Create postmortem doc when stable.

Ellen: handing off to daytime on-call (Leo) at 2815001400 for follow-up. I'll remain on the call for comms.

Leo: got it. will continue to monitor for 2 hours and then file the postmortem. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Maya: brief timeline for postmortem: detection 2815001228, mitigation started 2815001240, rollback 2815001295, edge-throttle 2815001310, incident declared stabilized 2815001425.

Priya: logging note for PM: add metric `retry_amplification_ratio` and alert when >1.5 for 5m.

Sam: saved mitigation commands to runbook: https://console.redwood/runbooks/retries-fallback-mitigation

Ellen: closing handoff. will ping again if we see regression.
